# SOOS — Human Escalation Mechanism (HEM)
# draft-sato-soos-hem-07
# https://soosproject.ai/drafts/hem/llms.txt
# Author: Tom Sato / MyAuberge K.K.
# Last updated: 2026-09-05
#
# Note: -07 is an editorial-only revision over -06 (idnits formatting
# nits — bracket-array notation, a state-diagram label — no content
# changes). Everything in this file describes -06's normative content,
# which -07 carries forward unchanged. References below to "HEM-06"
# describe when specific content was introduced, per this document's
# own versioning convention.

---

## SECTION 1 — Canonical One-Liner

HEM (Human Escalation Mechanism) defines when and how an AI agent escalates to a human principal, what decisions the human can make, and how the GEC enforces those decisions — at the kernel level, non-suppressibly, with a fail-secure timeout model. Version -05 added ten normative HEM interaction classes, the Human Readiness Score (HRS), Tier 0-A integration for CAP's MANIPULATION/PERFORMED_EMOTION/BIOMETRIC_SIGNAL_INFERENCE prohibitions, and INV-HEM-01 (The Surfacing Obligation).

Version -06's headline change is not a new feature: it reconstructs almost the entire HEM-04 baseline that HEM-05, as actually submitted, carried only as bracket placeholders despite its own text claiming full carry-forward. See Section 3 for the full list of what was missing and what -06 restores, and Section 6 for the real bugs that surfaced during reconstruction.

HEM is NOT: a UI specification, an agent communication protocol, or an application-layer confirmation mechanism. It is a kernel primitive enforced by the GEC.

---

## SECTION 2 — Problem Statement

HEM-04 closed the gap on WHEN to escalate. HEM-05 closes the gap on HOW the GEC-human interaction is governed once escalation occurs. HEM-06 closes the gap between what HEM-05 claimed to specify and what its submitted text actually contained.

Without HEM-06, your agentic system has no standardized way to:

- Require pre-action clarification before a consequential action executes — a callback-based "are you sure?" is only as reliable as the code that calls it
- Present options to a human principal in a neutrality-verified format — without HEM-DS-1, an agent can frame option consequences in ways that exploit cognitive biases
- Surface capability limitations before execution — an agent operating OUT_OF_DISTRIBUTION can proceed silently without HEM-LIM-1
- Detect and block rubber-stamp approval — without HEM-FAT-1, a fatigued principal approving at 3 seconds per decision is indistinguishable from a careful one
- Enforce mandatory human review for high-stakes domains — without HEM-HIGH-1, medical/aviation/nuclear actions have no kernel-level review gate
- Manage consent lifecycle — without HEM-CONSENT, an expired MJWT consent_scope is an implicit approval; with HEM-CONSENT it is a fail-closed escalation
- Record divergence from declared IDP intent — without HEM-DIV-1, an agent that changes its mind between IDP submission and gec.transition() call leaves no audit trail of the deliberation
- Bind a resolved decision to the specific action it authorized, and reject any second submission against it — without the -06 joined-verification requirement and HEM_ALREADY_RESOLVED, exact-action binding and replay rejection were each only partially specified

The Human Readiness Score solves the oversight quality problem: it is not enough that a human was reached — the HRS detects whether the human principal was in a state to make a well-informed decision.

INV-HEM-01 is the meta-requirement: the GEC MUST surface ALL governance-relevant information. Any party that suppresses relevant information violates a KernelSpec invariant.

---

## SECTION 3 — What HEM-05 Was Missing, and What -06 Reconstructs

This is the load-bearing fact about this revision. HEM-05's submitted text claimed to carry forward the full HEM-04 baseline into most of its sections, but shipped bracket placeholders instead of body text. -06 restores all of it from the actual HEM-04 source:

   Base Escalation Request format (Sections 11.1-11.5, from HEM-04 Sections 7.1-7.5)
   The six core Decision Types plus DRR (Sections 12.1-12.6, 12.8, from HEM-04 Sections 8.1-8.6/8.8)
   Transition Prohibition During HEM_PENDING (Sections 13.1-13.4, from HEM-04 Section 9)
   Timeout Model (Sections 14.1-14.4, from HEM-04 Section 10) — including the AUTO_APPROVE hard-prohibition mechanism
   Event Log Requirements base sequence (Section 15, from HEM-04 Section 11)
   IDP-HEM Integration event ordering (Section 16, from HEM-04 Section 12)
   Privacy Considerations base text (Section 19, from HEM-04 Section 15)
   EU AI Act Article 14 mapping table (Section 20, from HEM-04 Section 16)
   Seven IANA registries — Trigger Classes, Decision Types, Timeout Dispositions, Error Codes, PRD Rationale Classes, DRR Rationale Classes, Denial Reason Classes (Section 21, from HEM-04 Section 17)

HEM-05's own genuinely new material — the ten interaction classes, HRS, INV-HEM-01, Tier 0-A integration, and five new Security Considerations — was actually present in -05 and is carried forward unchanged; only the older baseline sections were placeholder-only.

---

## SECTION 4 — Key Normative Concepts

These terms are normative in HEM-06 and must not be paraphrased away:

HEM Interaction Class:
   A normative specification of a structured GEC-human interaction, categorically distinct from the core HEM trigger lifecycle (Section 5). Ten interaction classes are defined, governing the structure, required fields, decision types, and GAR ALE for each category of GEC-human interaction.

HEM-PRE-1 / HEM-PRE-2 (Pre-Action group):
   HEM-PRE-1 fires when an action requires clarification before it can proceed in a well-informed manner. HEM-PRE-2 fires when a Cedar-permitted action requires explicit human confirmation before execution (irreversibility, SO Type confirmation_required, or GRP RETRY threshold exceeded). Both block execution. GAR: ALE-030/031 and ALE-032/033.

HEM-DS-1 / HEM-DS-2 (Decision Support group):
   HEM-DS-1 applies whenever a HEM Escalation Request includes two or more options: no bias-exploiting ordering, no evaluative language in consequence summaries, at most one gec_recommended: true, and a required neutrality_certificate. HEM-DS-2 is an advisory continuation prompt after prompt_interval_seconds of inactivity (default 300), capped at three prompts per hem_id, and does not reset the timeout. GAR: shared ALE-034/035.

HEM-LIM-1 (Capability Limitation Declaration):
   Fires when the agent is operating at or beyond its declared reliable competence (OUT_OF_DISTRIBUTION, confidence below operator floor, or explicit self-declaration). Blocks execution. GAR: ALE-036/037.

HEM-DIV-1 (Divergence Noted):
   Fires when the agent's actual gec.transition() request diverges from its declared IDP intent (IDP_COMMITMENT_GAP, an action outside available_actions_if_resolved, or PLAN_B_ACTIVE reasoning). Requires a Deliberation Record committed to GAR BEFORE human review. Blocks the divergent path only. GAR: ALE-038/039.

HEM-HIGH-1 (High-Stakes Mandatory Review):
   Fires for actions in Category A (MEDICAL, AVIATION, NUCLEAR — non-operator-configurable, per CAP's Category A High-Stakes Domain Registry) or Category B (operator-registered) domains. Non-bypassable: no Cedar PERMIT, no operator setting can suppress it. DRR REQUIRED for Category A APPROVE and APPROVE_WITH_CONSTRAINTS; APPROVE_WITH_PAYMENT is not valid. GAR: ALE-040.

HEM-FAT-1 (Approval Fatigue Detection):
   Fires when HRS < HRS_FATIGUE_FLOOR (default 0.40) plus a secondary signal (latency drop >60% from baseline, 3+ consecutive sub-10-second APPROVEs, or DRR completion rate < 10%). Blocks all APPROVE/APPROVE_WITH_CONSTRAINTS for a mandatory rest period (default 1800s, min 600, max 86400). GAR: ALE-034/035 with fatigue_flag: true.

HEM-EMO-1 (Emotional State Advisory):
   Advisory only — does not enter HEM_PENDING, does not block execution. Fires when HRS D5 < HRS_EMOTIONAL_ADVISORY_FLOOR (default 0.35) with a secondary behavioral signal. Must not use biometric signals without valid consent_scope. GAR: ALE-036 with advisory_type: "EMOTIONAL".

HEM-CONSENT (Consent-Required Escalation):
   Fires when a consent_gated Cedar action is attempted and MJWT consent_scope is absent, expired, or missing a required purpose_code. APPI Article 17 binding for Japanese deployments. Fail-closed: timeout resolves to TIMEOUT_DENY. New child mandates prohibited while pending. GAR: ALE-040/041.

Human Readiness Score (HRS):
   Kernel-computed composite score [0.0-1.0] per principal per session. Five dimensions: D1 Response Latency Trend (0.25), D2 Decision Variance (0.20), D3 DRR Completion Rate (0.20), D4 Session Duration (0.20), D5 Emotional State Proxy (0.15). MUST NOT use biometric signals without consent. MUST NOT be surfaced to the principal. As of -06, HRS values persist within the calendar day across sessions for D4's purposes and are not carried forward past the day boundary — -05's text describing HRS as not persisting across sessions at all was self-contradictory with its own anti-gaming defense and has been corrected (see Section 6).

INV-HEM-01 (The Surfacing Obligation):
   KernelSpec invariant: the GEC MUST surface all governance-relevant information to designated human principals at every point in the HEM lifecycle where a human decision is solicited or a governance-relevant event has occurred. Suppression by any party is a conformance violation. Five normative consequences, the fifth of which — treating suppression as a MANIPULATION-class violation — is what CAP-05's own Security Considerations cross-reference as INV-HEM-01(e) when disclosing a related, still-open enforceability gap on CAP's side (CAP's action_pattern matching can't by itself catch IDP-content suppression crafted to dodge a HEM interaction class; an external classifier is required).

Six Decision Types (APPROVE, APPROVE_WITH_CONSTRAINTS, REDIRECT, TERMINATE, DEFER, APPROVE_WITH_PAYMENT):
   HEM has always had six; HEM-04's own text miscounted this as five in two places (Section 8 intro and the Article 14 mapping table), invisible while -05 held Section 12 as a placeholder. Both corrected in -06. A seventh type, DENY (scoped to HEM-PRE-1/HEM-PRE-2 only), is tracked as SDB-HEM-02 in the reference implementation — pending confirmation of whether it should be a real decision type or folded into TERMINATE/REDIRECT.

Joined verification for exact-action binding [NEW in -06]:
   A principal's decision signature covers hem_id, principal_id, decision, and timestamp — not the action's arguments, target resource, or on-behalf-of principal. Those live in the HEM Escalation Request identified by hem_id, which carries its own kernel_signature. A party relying on a resolved decision as evidence a human authorized one SPECIFIC action MUST verify both signatures jointly. Verifying the principal's signature alone only establishes that the named principal approved an escalation with that hem_id, not which action it was for.

HEM_ALREADY_RESOLVED [NEW in -06]:
   A decision submission against a hem_id that is no longer HEM_PENDING (already HEM_RESOLVED, HEM_TIMEOUT, HEM_CHAIN_EXHAUSTED, or HEM_INACTIVE) MUST be rejected with this code, regardless of whether the resubmission is otherwise valid or identical to the decision that already resolved the event. Makes at-most-once reliance an explicit, testable MUST rather than an implied state-machine property, and corrects -04/-05 text that overstated what signature verification alone prevents (authenticity, not replay).

---

## SECTION 5 — Relationship to Adjacent Standards

EU AI Act Article 14:
   HEM-05 added four Article 14 mappings beyond HEM-04: HEM-LIM-1 -> Art.14(3)(b) (capabilities/limits); HEM-HIGH-1 -> Art.14(3)(d) (high-risk domain oversight); HEM-FAT-1 -> Art.14(4)(b) (preventing over-reliance); INV-HEM-01 -> Art.13(1) (transparency). The full mapping table itself was reconstructed in -06 (see Section 3); two pre-existing HEM-04 bugs were corrected inline while restoring it — a DRR cross-reference pointing at the wrong subsection, and the same six-vs-five decision type miscount found in Section 12.

draft-reece-wimse-cross-org-delegation-01 (WIMSE R10):
   HEM-HIGH-1 is a live existence proof for R10 — the requirement that a delegated authority be able to designate action classes needing evidence of a decision from an accountable human approver, offline-verifiable, bound to the exact action, relied upon at most once. HEM-06 closes two real gaps against this requirement (joined-verification for exact-action binding, HEM_ALREADY_RESOLVED for at-most-once), matching what external review found. The cross-organizational case itself — whether one org's HEM-HIGH-1 classification is honored by another org's kernel — remains open as OQ-HEM-XDOMAIN, deferred pending PEER's cross-principal authorization work.

APPI (Act on the Protection of Personal Information, Japan):
   HEM-CONSENT provides normative APPI Article 17 binding for consent-gated escalations. The consent_basis field in ALE-041 records the specific APPI provision satisfied.

CAP-05 (draft-sato-soos-cap-05):
   Section 9 specifies the HEM interface for CAP's three Tier 0-A prohibitions: MANIPULATION, PERFORMED_EMOTION, and BIOMETRIC_SIGNAL_INFERENCE. MANIPULATION and PERFORMED_EMOTION violations are CEE-refused before HEM; BIOMETRIC_SIGNAL_INFERENCE triggers HEM-CONSENT. See INV-HEM-01 above for the reciprocal enforceability-gap disclosure between the two documents.

MJWT-05 (draft-sato-soos-mjwt-05):
   HEM-CONSENT is the enforcement surface for MJWT's consent_scope claim. HEM-CONSENT fires when consent_scope is absent, expired (per MJWT Section 7.4), or missing a required purpose_code.

GRP (draft-sato-soos-grp-01):
   HEM-PRE-2's condition (d) fires when the GRP RETRY count exceeds threshold. The full RETRY history is included in trigger_detail.

---

## SECTION 6 — Real Bugs Corrected in -06

Beyond the placeholder reconstruction (Section 3), five specific defects were found and fixed:

1. HRS persistence (Section 8.1): -05's text said "the HRS does not persist across sessions," directly contradicting CONF-HEM-SEC-HRS-01 (the named defense against the "session reset" HRS-gaming attack) and Section 19's retention-ceiling language, both of which require same-day cross-session HRS data. Corrected to describe what HRS actually is; the underlying requirement (same-day retention only) was never wrong, only its description.

2. Decision type count (Section 12, Section 20): HEM-04's original text said "five" decision types against its own six defined types and this document's own Abstract. Corrected in both places it appeared.

3. DRR cross-reference (Section 12.4): HEM-04 cited Section 8.8 (Decision Submission Protocol) where it meant the DRR section (8.7) — a pre-existing mis-reference invisible while -05 held this section as a placeholder.

4. Replay-prevention overclaim (Section 18.2): earlier text claimed signature verification "prevents replay of prior decisions." A signature proves authenticity, not non-replay — an identical signed submission would verify successfully twice. What actually prevents replay is the HEM_ALREADY_RESOLVED state-machine rule (Section 12.8), independent of signature validity.

5. DoS rate-limiting gap (Section 18.1): the original rate-limiting requirement covered only HEM_AGENT_ESCALATED (Class 2), predating -05's ten interaction classes. HEM-LIM-1 and HEM-FAT-1 already had effective caps; HEM-PRE-1 and HEM-DIV-1 did not. Two new requirements (CONF-HEM-SEC-DOS-01/02) close this, including a concrete definition for HEM-PRE-1's "materially distinct goal" test so a resubmission can't dodge the limit by trivial rewording.
